name: ZIMBABWE

flag.title: Flag of Zimbabwe
flag.note: Seven stripes; Zimbabwe Bird on triangle

lead: Zimbabwe is in southern Africa. It is named after its 900-year-old stone ruins. Victoria Falls roars so loudly you can hear it from 40 km away. Lake Kariba is the biggest man-made lake on Earth.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Zimbabwe sits on a high plateau called the Highveld, about 1,200 m up. Victoria Falls plunges 108 m and is 1.7 km wide. Its spray forms a permanent rainbow.
The Eastern Highlands rise to Mount Nyangani at 2,592 m. Frost forms there in winter. Lake Kariba, finished in 1959, stretches 280 km and powers millions of homes.
animals: Zimbabwe has the Big Five: lion, leopard, rhino, elephant and buffalo. Hwange National Park shelters around 40,000 elephants, one of Earth's most crowded elephant homes.
The African painted dog is one of Zimbabwe's most endangered animals. About 660 remain, in 86 packs. Nile crocodiles and hippos fill the Zambezi.
culture: The Shona people are about 70% of Zimbabwe. They have played the mbira, a thumb piano with metal keys, for over 1,000 years. Its music calls ancestors at healing ceremonies.
People scoop up sadza, a stiff maize porridge, and dip it in stew. The Ndebele paint bold patterns on house walls in black, white and red.
history: About 900 years ago, the Shona built a hilltop city of granite stones stacked with no cement. It held 18,000 people and traded gold with China. 'Zimbabwe' means 'great stone houses'.
British settlers arrived in 1890 and named the land Rhodesia. On 18 April 1980, Zimbabwe raised its flag. It was the last African country to win independence from Britain.
wows: Zimbabwe has 16 official languages, the most in any country.
In 2009, a 100 trillion dollar Zimbabwean note was worth about 40 US cents.
Victoria Falls' Shona name means 'The Smoke That Thunders'.
Lake Kariba holds about 180 cubic kilometres of water, the most of any man-made lake.
Zimbabwe has southern Africa's most rock-painting sites, made over 13,000 years.
No two African painted dogs have the same coat.
Great Zimbabwe covers 80 hectares (over 80 football pitches), the biggest stone ruin south of the Sahara.

myths.myth: Wild dogs are greedy and fight over food
myths.fact: Painted dogs share. Pups eat first, and the pack feeds sick dogs.

myths.myth: Victoria Falls has always had that name
myths.fact: No. Explorer David Livingstone named it after Queen Victoria in 1855.
